title: App Frozen No Longer Working

title: Good app overall, but Reminders integration appears broken
body: I like the app and the recipe management itself seems well designed, but there appears to be a current bug with the groceries/Apple Reminders integration. I’ve purchased the full version, granted Mela access to Reminders, and confirmed my Apple grocery list is set up correctly. However, Mela only shows its own “Mela” list as an option under Grocery settings, and adding ingredients from recipes does not actually create anything in Apple Reminders. I’m leaving this review mainly as a warning for anyone considering the app specifically because of the advertised Reminders integration. Hopefully it’s just a compatibility bug that gets fixed, because the rest of the app looks promising

title: Horrible user interface
body: It’s a great idea but I just spent roughly 45 minutes trying to put in one recipe from the Notes app. (Apple). The copy and paste function is one of the most frustrating features. And short of retyping the entire recipe into the app, I finally gave up. I had a rather complicated recipe with a long instruction list. I pasted the recipe into its entirety into the instruction area. Each time I tried to move the ingredients or nutrition from the spot it was pasted into to the appropriate place in the recipe template the copy function was impossible to use. Or rather the selection of the text itself. You can only copy the length of the screen. Scrolling to copy is impossible. The keyboard stays active and gives only a tiny area to copy. You can’t dismiss the keyboard or the whole copy disappears. Why in the heck would I want to use an app when I can organize things by name, title etc in an app like Notes? I have hundreds of recipes I have written and more I have found and collected. They are already typed so why is it so hard to put them into this Mela app? I can’t recommend at all.

title: Good but behind
body: While Mela is a perfectly fine recipe manager application, it is FAR outpaced by competition. The app itself feels fairly outdated in general, while lacking great easy import features like importing from websites or videos. Adding groceries will require a specific Mela tab in reminders, not allowing the user to add groceries to their own shopping or groceries list. If you’re looking for a bare-bones recipe list, this may do it for you. However the often requests to upgrade to a pro membership (which I can’t fathom what that even adds that would be worth it) may be annoying. Honestly, a Notes tab may be a better way to go… and it’s completely free.

title: Nearly the best. Falls short on recipe organization features.
body: I really want to love this app and it has so much going for it. It is easy to add recipes, they look beautiful, it is super easy to half recipes, and the grocery list function is actually really helpful. But once you add a decent number of recipes, Mela’s weaknesses in organization really come out and get annoying. The category labeling feature is clumsy and frustrating to use. You can add new category labels, but only from within a recipe. And if you want to change your labels later to better organize your growing recipe library, be prepared to spend a lot of time on this. You can only click one category at a time when designating categories from within a recipe. And once a category label is created, you can never delete that label from your list! It would be nice to be able to open up a category and either add or remove recipes from there. It would also be nice to have a way to easily switch between multiple open recipes because when you are in the middle of cooking one recipe and have to check a second recipe, there are just too many steps to find the first one again! I really hope that the developers of this app aren’t going to take their relative success and leave good enough alone. I will keep crossing my fingers for useful updates to Mela’s ability to organize and access my recipe library.

title: Good but lacking in usability
body: I really like this app, the UI is beautiful to look at, which is the primary reason I chose Mela over other apps that have much stronger features. I appreciate the simplicity, however there are some features I feel could be added to enhance the user experience without compromising the simplicity. • ability to import a url INSIDE of the app instead of just through safari • ability to rearrange the grocery list • option to show a small photo/icon of the chosen recipe in the meal planning section • Additionally, I sometimes add YouTube links in the notes and would appreciate notes to recognize this and create a hyperlink. I see this app has not been updated in over a year, I really hope it hasn’t been abandoned. I would hate to have to use an ugly app lol, but many of them are advancing far beyond what Mela is currently capable of and I’m starting to think I would be better off with an intuitive UI then a pretty one.

title: Inaccessible organization but impressive otherwise
body: I've tried a bunch of recipe apps and this one is a standout, overall well worth the price, though some organizational features are unintuitive and lacking. Primarily, the main navigational pane that lets you filter views is weirdly inaccessible. It would be intuitive if I could access the pane by swiping from the left side of the screen, but instead, you have to locate one of two small buttons in the corners. Similarly, the sorting options are very inaccessible, you have to tap an element near the bottom of the screen that is TINY and also hard to see. It'd make more sense and be more consistent with other apps if the sorting options were under the ellipsis menu (e.g. in Apple Notes) instead. The "new recipe" function also 100% deserves its own button on the main page instead of being thrown into the navigational pane. Similar to Paprika, Crouton, Umami, a plus sign button in the upper right corner could let me select between scanning, manual add, or adding a recipe from a URL. I could then add recipes immediately, instead of having to once again pull up the frustratingly placed navigational pane. The category/tag function is great, but when viewing a tag, there's no way to: edit/rename the current tag, quickly get back to the all recipes view, or select and view multiple tags. I wish I could filter for recipes that are both "soup" and "vegan" for example, and that there was generally a faster way to select/switch between tags besides tapping in the corner, scrolling, and selecting a different tag. I wish the ellipsis menu in a tag view had tag-specific edit options like rename and delete. There's also no way to rate recipes, batch select/edit multiple recipes (e.g. to add a certain tag), categorize groceries or make multiple grocery lists e.g. for different stores, or add your own notes (separate from the notes of the recipe itself). Lastly, neither the coral pink in light mode nor the dandelion yellow in dark mode with white text are super easy on the eyes, even with the "increase contrast" option on. I write all of this because this is a fantastic app otherwise. It syncs well, feels smooth, has seamless recipe import and a ton of great features. I hope it continues to improve.

body: Hard to really know if I can’t import my recipes from Crouton. I see there is an import option but it doesn’t have any information on what kind of formats are supported. Give me a way to move my data and I might buy your app.

body: Why do I have to scroll alllllllll the way back to the top to find the search bar again? It should be static at the top of the recipe lists. This is my only real complaint but it’s super annoying because I have 100s of recipes.

title: Nice app but…
body: Disappointed that I now have to pay an extra $10 for the MacOS app after already paying $5 for the iOS version. :(

title: Please add a manual “Sync Now” feature!
body: I love, love this app! Moved over from another similar app I had been using for several years; however, the sync on Mela is very inconsistent. I have not added a recipe in over a week but all 3 of my devices have different numbers of recipes. Also, my “Want to cook” list on my iPad has 25 recipes in it while there are only 4 on my MacBook Pro, while my phone is showing 12. Has been that way for a week. Please, please, add a “sync now” button to push the sync across devices or improve the syncing to trigger it every time the app is opened. Super frustrating.

title: Best cooking app, BUT —
body: I absolutely love this cookbook app! It’s the simplest and most beautifully designed cookbook app on the App Store, and it’s so affordable. I do have a few suggestions for improvement. It would be great to add safeguards to make it harder to accidentally delete recipes or other items, or at least include a way to recover deleted content. Customization options for colors in the menu and background, as well as the ability to add custom covers or choose from in-app designs, would be amazing. I’d also love the option to share public links to my cookbook or specific recipes in a way that others can view but not edit or delete. Being able to create multiple cookbooks within the app, select which recipes to include, customize their order, and add interactive features like tappable links or stickers to navigate between recipes would make the app even better. This app also really needs a conversion calculator and a conversion chart. Thank you for creating such a fantastic app—these updates would make it perfect!

title: Was amazing starting to go downhill
body: If you want a recipe book app for just you this is definitely it. Personally I landed on this app over other apps like it because it had a great family share feature. Everyone in my house uses Apple devices so no worries about compatibility. Started out great I imported about 400 family recipes my wife inherited. Set her and my two oldest kids up with the paid version. And everything worked great. Anyone who added a recipe to the app was synced with everyone else. Everyone could see the calendar and whoever’s turn to cook just had to look. Then it start to get buggy. First my wife couldn’t add recipes others could see in the list. Then we could see the meal she added to the calendar but not the recipe. This kept degrading over time and now updates from anyone doesn’t sync with each other. Honestly if I didn’t have over a 1000 recipes in here I’d try a different app

title: A great start, but some features fall short.
body: This app has a lovely interface and is very user friendly in the browse and feeds features and it scrapes recipes from the Internet flawlessly. However there are some quirks that are big drawbacks and make some of the features impractical. 1) recipe categories- I don’t believe there is a way to edit all of the categories you create. When creating a new recipe you can only add a category by typing in the name and then categories you have previously created will show up above it, in the same format as spell check does. You also create new categories this way. If you accidentally create a duplicate category, there is no screen you can go to to edit all the categories and delete ones you don’t need. 2) The feature for creating a new recipe by taking a picture of a hard copy is not usable. When you scan the photo, you are instructed to select the text and choose a type of text. So you drag a box around the ingredients, for example, and select ingredients from the drop down. I could not find a way to do a second selection and choose a different text type as well for, say, the instructions. So, you continue to the next step and it uploads only the ingredients. I then looked for another option to take a new photo and upload the instructions or the title, but there is no way to do that. Essentially, if you want to scan a recipe in you can only scan in either the title, ingredients, or the instructions. You can’t upload all 3, which makes it unusable without manually entering a significant amount of text. If these features could be fixed, this would be the best app of its kind.

title: Great at first, now aggravating
body: My wife and I use this app with me as the owner. We share under our iCloud family. The app used to work great, until recently any recipe my wife adds to our shared list doesn’t show up on my app. It’s aggravating when she asks me to make a meal that she’s added to Mela, and go to look for it under most recent, and it’s not there. We have a difference of 3 recipes right now, that I assume will only get larger as time goes on. Considering deleting this app, an app I paid for and regret ever putting my faith in to “make life simpler”

title: Issue scanning if there’s more than one photo/ page?
body: I can’t seem to figure out what I’m doing wrong so I think it’s an issue with the app. If you’re scanning in a recipe from a photo/ camera, the first page works fine, and then any additional pages or photos don’t. It won’t offer the same option to add/ scan a second page. So you just add another photo, and it just adds it as a photo, without running you thru the option to select the text or photo on the page and add those details. So it doesn’t seem to really work for importing recipes from physical cookbooks and photos if they are more than one page, which…makes it pretty unusable.

title: More recipes
body: It only allows you to save 10 recipes in the free version ._.

title: Good but missing important features
body: This is a pretty good recipe app, but it has a ways to go. Some features I’d like to see: - Better iCloud integration. Currently, there is a bug where grocery lists made on the app don’t automatically sync with the phone app. In order to do this I have to turn iCloud syncing off and then turn it on again - Saved shopping lists. I have a lot of items I buy regularly but that aren’t part of any particular recipe. I’d like a way to save certain items as shopping list favorites so I can add them to new lists easily - Organized shopping lists. Currently the grocery lists are just a jumble of items. It’d be nice to have them sorted by aisle or department (this is a feature that Samsung Food/Whisk does well)

title: Missing Key Things
body: The app has great look but it’s missing key things like sorting the recipes by categories (appetizer, breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner, etc..). Also, when importing ingredients to shopping list, it doesn’t categorize it either (produce, meats, dairy, etc..). It simply copies the ingredient list from every recipe. Not helpful at all.

title: Full calendar access suddenly required
body: I loved this app. I used it for over a year. I would happily pay a subscription fee. It’s gorgeous and easy to navigate, and I love having food blog feeds integrated into the UX. However, in December or early January, the app changed from requiring “add only” calendar access to requiring full read+add access. I can’t give full read access to my calendars. I figured I’d use the internal calendar and manually add my planned meals to my Google calendar. But nope. Once you reject full calendar access, the entire calendaring function disappears. It’s made a beautiful, seamless app experience extremely frustrating. I emailed the developer, and received no response.

title: Nice but …
body: Possibly the nicest recipe app. Looks good and has good features. Reasonable price, also. However, there are some bugs and feature limitations. Repeated emails to the developer have received no response. ?????

title: Nope
body: I wanted to like this app, it being so highly rated. My favorite cookbook app is no longer supported and is not in the app store, so I was looking for a new one. This just isn’t it. Far too much real estate is taken up by the title of the recipe and the list of recipes column, with the ingredients list almost falling off the page on the left. The only way I could successfully transfer a recipe without retyping it by hand was to email it to myself and save the pdf to Files, then import it into this app. Not practical for the over 1,000 recipes I have collected. Looking for something a bit more customizable, too. The font choices do not seem to work on the free version, and there are only three, so I don’t know why they bothered.

title: Love it mostly, but…
body: When I scan a recipe from a magazine or a cookbook to put into the app, there’s no way to view it full screen or zoom in to read it better when I access it. So it’s basically useless to me for that since it’s not big enough to read. Am I missing something?? It would be very tedious to take all of those kinds of recipes and input them manually. But I do love the format and layout for saving recipes that are taken from the Internet and added to the app.

title: Good app, customer service seems nonexistent
body: I think the app is good. There are some features I might like to see with it, but not a deal breaker. Would probably give it 4 or 5 stars if they ever replied to emails. I sent one requesting features and another asking questions they have not replied. One in February and one about 4 days ago.

Additionally, it would be helpful if the groceries list could be organized by type (produce, bakery, frozen, etc) for shopping ease and noted with which recipe the ingredient is for. Looking forward to updates versions bc it is such a beautiful app!

body: OCR is absolutely horrible. Mixes up lines and word order constantly, such that I am essentially forced to manually input recipes whenever I try to scan them from a cookbook. Very frustrating.

title: Yellow is Fugly
body: Your use of yellow is FUGLY. Please use something less abusive to the eyes. Or let is choose.

title: Great app but needs its own storage, not iCloud
body: I love the design of the app but really disappointed since I paid for the Mac and OS apps to find they have don’t have their own storage and use iCloud instead. The problem with that is that for people like me where my laptop is my work computer, my iCloud is turned off so the recipe sharing doesn’t work at all. Which is a massive problem. I have this problem with NO other paid apps I use since they know sync is a key feature and didn’t cheap out and use iCloud.

title: Wonderful App; Missing Core Sync Feature
body: I truly love this app but unlike Paprika I cannot share recipes with my partner. This is unfortunately a table stakes feature for me as I need to coordinate meal planning with my partner.

title: Really good recipe app!
body: I love this recipe app and it’s changed my life! It’s so nice to have all my recipes in one place and it has made meal planning and grocery shopping much easier. I opted to try this one instead of recipe keeper (the app lots of my friends use) because this one had a lower upfront cost and overall it looks and feels much nicer. Pros: - Great user interface! Looks and feels like a really nice app - One upfront cost, no subscription - has most other features you’d expect from a recipe app The only con that I’ve encountered (reason for 4 stars) is that I wish I could filter by more than one category at a time. For example, I have a dairy-free category and a gluten-free category. I wish that I could filter by both at the same time, but currently I can only do one or the other. Even better if I were able to filter by as many categories as I wanted to (e.g., soups, chicken, gluten free, and dairy free to get all recipes fitting in all of these categories). This is my main feature request, otherwise this app works great and I’m fairly happy to trade the beautiful UI for slightly less functionality compared to recipe keeper. Edit to add: I also wish I could click on the pictures to make them full screen and zoom in. A lot of my pictures are from recipe notecards and I sometimes want to double check the original picture.

title: Missing ability to Scale Recipe
body: Beautifully designed app and quite functional. But when it comes to cooking, we need a feature to scale the original recipe to be 1/2 or 2 times depending on how many guests we have! Currently I have to manually multiply myself but would love for the app to have this ability.

title: Almost perfect
body: This is the best recipe management app I’ve ever used. The only feature I wish it had is the ability to search for a new recipe from any view. Usually when I open the app, it’s showing the recipe I’ve most recently prepared, so I have to scroll all the way back to the top of the list to search for the next one. I have a pretty long list of recipes, so this gets annoying. Please consider adding this feature! Thanks!

title: favorite recipe app, but….
body: i love this app but i do really wish it was still being updated because there are several features i would really love to have.

title: Love this app SO much...
body: I use Mela every sine day, both to collect new recipes and for meal planning and cooking. And the RSS feature is genius! My one request is for a more robust scraping capability on sites like Instagram. I follow numerous cooking profiles and collect recipes from them. Mela has gotten a lot better at capturing such recipes but there is still probably about a third of what I want to save that I end up saving with a competitor app that is much more capable at this. Mela is far superior and much more enjoyable to use, and I would love to discard the other app and keep all my digital recipes in Mela.

title: Worthwhile Recipe App
body: Update: 05/16/2026 I’ve gotten pretty decent in managing my files; however, Editing the categories to remove accidental category made or edit an existing one I haven’t been able to do. If I correct the category in error, it just makes a new category entry. I like things neat and fairly easy; I don’t want my mistakes still available to choose from the list. I just got the app today and immediately began importing my recipes. The scan option works pretty decent, love the import option from websites, and love being able to assign categories. The only complaint I have so far is I haven’t been able to import any of my pdf file recipes. The message I get when trying says “no recipe found”. But for the cost, it’s still worth having especially since when I travel to help care for my Mom I can take my favorite recipes along that I may cook without all the hassle. Wish I understood why the pdf import function doesn’t work with either my Google drive or Dropbox, which is where I have almost all my electronic recipes currently stored.

title: More needed
body: This is a great app. Been using it for several years. But it needs to grow up and work with instagram and facebook to grab those recipes we like. But it’s still worth it. Love it and will continue to is it.

title: Almost perfect recipe manager
body: This app is a wonderful tool to keep and import recipes though once you have more than about five dozen recipes, it’s challenging to find anything, there’s no search function, and no auto categorization, so unless you remember the original name of the recipe, it takes too long to find it

title: Looks promising.
body: This app does what I wish Pestle did which is have a great meal planning feature which separates Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner for calendar blocking. I even appreciate the small widget which looks amazing. The only thing this app lacks is the Start Cooking feature that Pestle has which is amazing. This app does it in a barebones way.

title: Amazing for saving recipes, but lacking features for meal planning
body: It’s so nice to pull recipes from websites without having to scroll through paragraphs and ads. It makes the recipe search so efficient! However, I wish the grocery list was categorized and allowed for pantry tracking. If these two features were added, this would be the ultimate meal planning app. I would make another one-time purchase for either of these features if they were added. Another plus would be receipt scanning.

title: Quite good but not perfect
body: I’d like to see scanned recipes pass though a formatting step (GPT?) that can put the formatting right for me by deleting new lines etc after I scan from a PDF. I’d also like to see a GPT-powered process for PDFs as a whole so I don’t have to select anything at all, it should just import automatically. Doesn’t support the recipe keeper website which makes migration annoying. I’d like to share feeds and grocery lists with my partner too, not just recipes. There’s also a bug in the recipe scaling: put in 1 13.5oz cans of coconut milk. This doubles to 2 27oz cans of coconut milk! This is bad! 4x instead of 2x! I’d suggest adjusting the regex I assume is being used to get the amounts to not capture the oz number in this case. I’d also really like to see sorting for groceries list into sections so it’s easier to shop. Edit: found a way to sync groceries! From one account, share the Mela Reminders list to the other. Then delete any unshared Mela list and boom it uses the shared one. This works well, but obviously is not obvious. Same for calendars.

title: Great app
body: Simple app with, thankfully, no subscription or add on fees and even allows family sharing. So nice. Easy to share recipes and cookbooks. Clean, readable interface. Great at clipping recipes off web. Grocery list is slightly clunky when adding the same item from different recipes. Would be nice to be able to star rate individual recipes.

title: Please add a search feature!
body: I used to bookmark recipes into category folders but this app makes managing my recipes much easier. I would love to have a search/filter feature added, so I could do a keyword across all categories or within one category. For example, if I am in a Cakes category, it would be helpful to be able to filter results to a specific ingredient, e.g. “chocolate”, to show me only cakes that included chocolate. Multi-word filters are even better, if I’m trying to find a recipe that uses several ingredients, such as chicken, tomato, mushrooms.

title: Best Recipe App?
body: I really like Mela. The only reason I don’t rate a 5 star is the format and flexibility of the Grocery List. I use Apple Notes for all my shopping lists. I would like to be able to copy and paste Melas Grocery List into Notes. You cannot select the entire list and copy and paste.

title: Amazing but wishing for one more feature
body: The layout and functionality of this app is amazing. It makes meal planning super simple. My wife and I share a recipe collection and try to share a calendar to do meal planning for the week together. The app doesn’t provide much for calendar sync between two accounts. We are able to each share our iCloud calendar with each other but have had some issues with functionality. It would be nice to be able to share the calendar in the app just as we can share the recipe collection. Being said we have really enjoyed the app and plan to use it for a long time.

title: Enjoying it
body: Really like it but wondering if you’ll be adding the ability to update the app icon? Would love a few different options, even just color variations.

title: AMAZING - but
body: I love this app so much, wish my mom could use it but she doesn’t have an iPhone - the only thing I’ve come to want from this app is maybe like a spot where recommended “feeds” otherwise I don’t use it. But most importantly i wish the grocery list was categorized and or bundled up multiples from more than one recipe.

title: Nearly feature complete
body: I use this app multiple times a week to store recipes we like. It makes importing them easy. It does have some missing tools I’d love to see incorporated. Expanded conversion tools to adjust the scale or convert a unit. Merged grocery lists - group, sort and it would be awesome to partner with a grocery store to streamline the grocery shopping process. Providing users with tools to reduce waste in their meal planning and sourcing. Nutrition and budget tuning - provide users with tools that help them tune their shopping habits to improve health and reduce waste.

title: PLEASE ADD FEATURE
body: I’d give this app 6 stars if they would add one feature: The ability to choose which category a recipe goes into before adding the recipe to the app. Besides that, this app is a game changer. Especially for people with ADHD (me). I LOVE the cook mode. More specifically, I love being able to toggle back and forth between the cooking instructions and the ingredients and being able to check them off as you go.

title: Please make browser/PC app!
body: Perfect for a home chef! I’m so glad I found this app and that I never have to go back to Pinterest for storing my recipes. I can easily capture recipes from a variety of websites, and can add them manually as well. I had the apps for both iOS and MacOS. I recently switched from a Mac to PC and unfortunately now only have Mela on my phone/iPad, and I really miss the functionality of using it on my desktop. Please make a browser/PC version!! 🥲

title: Very pleasing ui
body: Needs improvement in the Ingredients measurements, distinguish between quantities and measurements such as tablespoon and cup. so when adding to groceries will be clean.

title: Almost perfect
body: Pros: - Affordable pay once model - Clean minimalist UI - Fast sync between devices - Cooking mode - Markdown export - Grocery list - Reminders integration - Meal planning - Calendar integration - In-app browser - Feeds This that will make this the perfect recipe manager app: - Separate categories & tags - Being able to add foods that are not recipes within the app to calendar / meal plan - Being able to see carbs & calories at the top of

title: Gorgeous, but falls a little short
body: First, the best things about it… (1) look and feel: so good. It’s the kind of app you WANT to a reason to use (2) camera for recipe capture: I use it to pull quickly recipes out of my beloved cookbooks The limitations… (1) Paprika, which I have used for maybe a decade now, has a really nice “pin” location where you can collect recipes you are considering or actively working on. It’s easy to access- especially while cooking multiple recipes at once. Mela doesn’t have anything like this. Cook mode in Mela DOES have multiple recipes, but the UI for this is flawed and more importantly you can’t scale recipes in this mode. Kind of worthless honestly, bc of that. (2) Groceries also has some real limitations compared to Paprika. As far as I can tell, you can’t manage multiple lists (like multiple grocery stores). Summary: Very pretty app, with one piece of functionality being next level (camera capture) but the rest of it falling short of the title holder in this category: Paprika.

title: Great app
body: Wish there was an option to add videos.

title: Beautiful design
body: I really enjoy the interface of the app the design is beautiful. The way it’s set up to take you through the recipe while you’re cooking is very convenient you can swipe back and forth between instructions and ingredients and it highlight the step you’re currently on in the instructions. I love the layout it’s very visually appealing. There’s some features I wish it had though like scanning a recipe from a photo already on your phone I also want more widgets like favorite recipes or maybe quick add buttons. But overall I really enjoy the app even though it has less features than similar apps I still prefer to wait for this app to add features when the recipe walkthrough is as easy as it is.

title: Great app
body: Great app. I wish it honored markdown for formatting. ## or ** or bullet points don’t work.

title: So close to perfect
body: I used to use Paprika religiously until I found Mela. Design wise it’s incredibly well made, but it falls short in a few ways. Importing from a website is better than Paprika but still not fool proof. Categories are somewhat haphazardly implemented and there is no way to nest or organize your categories which creates a very long scrollable list, and without going into this list and finding a category, there’s no way to filter. Would be great if you could filter by category in the top search, or search through existing categories. I also don’t love the way images work as if you have a recipe as a photo and want to refer to that, there is no way to maximize the image by tapping which seems like a missed opportunity. In general the app seems like it’s in a bit of a maintenance mode, which is disappointing, but it’s still very good. I’ve tried making these suggestions directly to the developer but never received a response, so the dev is not exactly responsive.

title: Almost perfect!
body: I have downloaded so many meal planning apps in the past week and this does 95% of what I’m looking for! ✔️calendar integration where I can move the meal (it would be awesome if it was automatically scheduled for prep & cook time, but I can manually change that) ✔️ integrates with reminders for my shopping list ✔️ easy to use recipe import 😐the scaling recipe is very basic double, half etc. some of the apps I’ve used gave the ability to scale by number of servings (ie: recipe is for 4 servings, but you need 5)… The only major things missing: ❌ widgets offered are very basic, I like a week overview, not just the next meal ❌ Can’t rate recipes. Also, you can leave notes, but those only appear on the calendar from what I can tell so far, so they won’t do any good next time you make it. I’d also love it if it saved when the last time a recipe was made. Originally, I thought there was no way to categorize recipes, but I found it!

title: Only one drawback. Otherwise perfect
body: The only pitfall is that imports could use more AI. Even from a website the importer doesn’t always get prep/cook/total times right. AI for importing from a document or a picture would be nice too, to make it more automatic. Great price. Small one-time payment instead of a repeated large payment. Beautiful. Makes baking and cooking significantly more satisfying. Great organization system. Having cookbooks/folders is always messy and makes my eye twitch every time a recipe could belong in multiple cookbooks/folders at once. Having only tags solves this problem. And tagging is easy in this app. Type and autofill or select from a dropdown menu. Compatible. Precisely efficient at creating recipes from websites, documents, photos, etc. Why do people use Paprika when there’s this app??

title: Worthwhile App
body: The app is great for people like me who like to save recipes from websites across the internet. The app is great for removing the wordiness from blogs and just transferring the main parts of the recipe. If there were a few enhancements this would be a close to perfect app. One, would be different rating systems to rate the recipes you have done and be able to see it at a glance. For example, thumbs up or down to tell if you like the recipe or not, and a difficulty scale to remember at a glance if the recipe was easy or hard to execute. If a recipe came out bad or good you could mark it and know it to either continue using it or maybe making adjustments or improvements. It would also be nice to group recipes by the rating as well. Two, would be a batch way to edit the categories of multiple recipes at a time. Finally, in each section of the recipe, e.g. the instructions, ingredients, etc., more editing controls would be nice. For example, having a fixed “select all” button, and a “copy”, “paste”, and “cut”button like the cook time, prep time, and total time sections have. Despite, lacking these enhancements it is still a great app and I am glad I purchased it.

title: ADHD friendly, easy to use, great for families
body: First, we have an ADHD household that is easily distracted or gets overwhelmed with poorly laid out directions and visual clutter. The layout and design of the app, as well as the focused cooking modes on phone and tablets are extremely helpful and well thought out. It is easy to import recipes that look interesting. I switched over from Paprika several years ago, and am very happy with the switch. Paprika is also a great and robust app. My reason for switching was purely because of aesthetics and trying to get an app that everyone in the family can easily use. I do have some feature requests though: - I would love a “tile” view on tablet and iPhone that is image focused. There’s a lot of wasted space on the tablet if I’m just browsing recipes to figure out what I want. I can only see 7 entries in landscape mode, and I’d love to see 20-30 cards with just picture and title. - I’d love for the timers to be louder or somehow sync across my devices - if my watch could yell at me (because ADHD and I walk away from things) - I’d love a “command center” mode for the calendar view or a print view - let me see a week’s worth of meal planning, or better yet a month’s with images (if I want) so I can either send the pdf/image to my family, or print it and put it on the fridge. I would be happy with a week view - Paprika was really good at keeping track of what was in my pantry, and combining ingredients for easier shopping. It would be nice if Mela could also do these things. I don’t need 4 different entries telling me I need various amounts of garlic. Just tell me the total so I need for this shopping trip

title: Recipes at your fingertips
body: I never pay for apps and I paid for this one. Totally worth it - I have over 2K recipes saved. I can decide what I want to eat when I am leaving work since I can just scroll and find what I want to cook. And a big bonus is being able to adjust the recipe size. The two small issues I have is that I can’t mark if I have already cooked something. And I can’t search recipes by ingredient.

title: Loving it so far besides one thing
body: Absolutely obsessed with the app my only gripe is that it’s always stuck on All recipes and it Makes the app feel cluttered. Would love to be able to have all my categories shown at first then I could select through them. But seems there isn’t a way to do that with out using the drop downs so whenever I entered the app it’s just all my recipes. Would love that extra layer of organization

title: Great app with potential
body: The scanning, search, and ease of use are phenomenal. This is my favorite recipe manager I’ve tried, and I’d highly recommend it. Unfortunately, the feature to have a shared cookbook with family members or a partner is not working. This was the core feature I was looking for in a recipe app. Some other wishlist items: - the ability to click on the photos to focus/enlarge. I save the full recipes as a photo, just in case, but it is rather useless - the ability to “group by” such as by source (like cookbooks) Also, the app frequently crashes, so I’ve learned to save early and often. If I’m creating a recipe from a scan, there are high odds it’ll crash after the text is imported and I’m trying to add a photo.

title: Fantastic!
body: I love this app so much. We use it everyday in the kitchen. My only complaint is that the search feature doesn’t save the filter selection. I always search by recipe name and including ingredient matches in the results isn’t what I need. I wish my filter selection would stick so I don’t have to deselect “ingredients” every search.

title: I love this app, but can it replace paprika?
body: First off, I would like to say that the aesthetic and design of this app is spot on. I love the layout, the choice of font, and how the recipe is displayed. The recipe importer is fantastic, the best recipe importer of any app that I’ve ever used. I love that I can take a picture from a book. I can snip a website. I can scan a recipe card. Whatever format your recipes in, this app can import them in someway. The sharing of your recipe collection with other users, such as family members or friends is also a much welcome to benefit! after importing quite a few recipes, the first thing that you’ll notice is the navigation can be a bit wonky, for example, in order to search for a recipe if you’ve scrolled down the list of recipes you need to scroll all the way back up to the top to get to the search bar. It would be nice if a search bar lived at the top permanently. When it comes to the organization of recipes, I can’t complain much however I do miss the hierarchy of the folder, structure in paprika, which makes it a little bit easier to find what I’m looking for. When inside the recipe specifically in Cook mode, it would be beneficial if the ingredients in the text would highlight as tappable Text, in which case would display the amount of ingredient from the ingredient list. As far as meal planning and groceries go, it would be nice to be able to put your meal plan together and then select the days that you want to build a grocery list for and send all of those ingredients to your grocery list and before fully adding everything combine the similar items and if needed open a prompt to correct any mismatches or approve any possible matches so your grocery list doesn’t have several of the same items in it. Having a separate spot in the app where you can include things from your pantry, such as spices that you don’t need to purchase on a regular basis that would stop those ingredients from being added to your grocery list would be nice. Overall, I would say this app has definitely become my go to in terms of the cooking mode, but unfortunately, I am still using paprika because the meal planning and grocery list is just to stressful of a task to keep up with. The way paprika allows you to create a meal plan export the entire meal plan to your grocery list and before adding everything asks you what needs to be combined what don’t you need, etc. makes the experience much more pleasurable. I would still recommend this app to anybody that wants a decent recipe app and maybe doesn’t need the meal planning features of it. I hope some of these recommendations will make it into future updates, but for now I will say this App is definitely one of the best.

title: Almost perfect! Missing one key feature
body: I’ve tried a handful of similar apps for recipe collecting and meal planning, and hands down Mela is the best! I love the UI, the recipe importer works incredibly well, and I love that Mela integrates with Apple Reminders and Calendar and doesn’t force you to be locked into storing data that is only accessible in their app. There is one feature missing that would certainly make this a 5 star app: adding a meal that is not a recipe into the meal planning section. For example, let’s say one night I’m planning on eating a frozen pizza. Currently, if I were to add that in my meal calendar, it’s not supported, since I don’t have a frozen pizza recipe. The workaround would be to manually add frozen pizza as a meal to the Mela calendar via Apple Calendar, but this is not ideal and breaks the flow of planning out the entire week in Mela. Alternatively you could create a recipe for frozen pizza, but that is also not ideal since those types of entries aren’t true recipes and will add up over time. If the developer can add adding an entry to the Calendar from the app and not requiring it to be an existing recipe, then this would be the perfect app and definitely would be a 5/5 for me!

title: A superb app with some room for improvement
body: This is a wonderful app. It's super hand and well designed. I love the ability to import recipes from web pages. Being able to instantly add ingredients to the grocery list is extremely handy. The syncing between devices works pretty well too. I have two main issues with the app that I'd love to see fixed. First, the keyboard in the grocery list doesn't have any spell check or suggestions, so there's no auto correction, making it easy to make mistakes. This isn't a huge problem, just more of an annoyance. The other issue that is much more of a problem is that there's no way to manually organize groceries in the list. You can technically do it through the reminders app, which is how the groceries are stored, but then sometimes Mela will "reset" the order, undoing any of the organization. This happened this morning where I had organized my list to make sense for my local store, but when I got to the store, Mela had reset the order for everything, causing me to lose track of the different items and take much more time double-checking everything I needed. I'd love to see this fixed where the ordering is persisted. All in all this is a great app and I recommend it. I think those two improvements will make it that much better.

title: Can’t categorize when sharing-have to reopen app
body: I’ve used Mela extensively. So the one disadvantage of Mela is that when sharing, you can’t add a category. You have to add to Mela then it returns to the web recipe. The additional step is you have to reopen Mela to add the recipe just shared to a category and to edit. It’s an extra unnecessary step. Paprika allows you to add a category/edit after sharing. The advantage of Mela is being able to share recipes from the New York Times cooking app and Mela adds the Introduction recipe notes which Paprika doesn’t. Oh how nice it would be to have the best of both of these very good recipe apps.

title: Aesthetic & Clean App
body: Amazing cooking app and love the simple interface. Only thing I would love have added to this app is the ability to auto-convert units or scale up something in the recipe like serving sizes. Minus this one feature love the uncluttered feel of the app

title: The best recipe app on iOS and macOS
body: Hands-down the best recipe app on iOS and macOS. It removes the life story that accompanies nearly every recipe now, and is a beautiful and well made app. It has great features like export and sharing, and everything is backed up and synced on iCloud. If it’s the best, why 4-stars you might be asking? And well, it’s because there are a few rough edges. As my collection of recipes has grown, the categories function has become too simple to use effectively in my opinion. It needs a “tags” feature added too. If that is added, it will be an instant 5-starts. Another nice to have would be a function to sort by recipes based on ingredients, but I can understand that is a hard function to build.

title: Sharing outside of Apple is non existent
body: Love the app overall - website parsing is ridiculously fast and accurate, UI is great, and generally fun to use. Two questions - Is there a way to see in the grocery list (in the app) which recipe the ingredient came from? This is a big feature I miss from other meal planning apps and an important one too. - Currently I see 0 ways to share a grocery list to a non iOS/MacOS friend without using iCloud. Any plans to just at least allow exporting a simple list into text or something like that? Big bummer in terms of using with family if we’re not all in iOS. This might be the biggest reason for me to stop using this app (even bought the MacOs version)

title: Pretty good
body: Pretty good recipe planner. I love the integrated “feed” feature for my favorite blogs. I’d love if you could import multiple images to scan recipes instead of just one. It would also be nice to select multiple & edit at once. For Example if you input 5 recipes from a cookbook, to select all and add the source vs having to do that separately.

title: At First, I loved it, and then….
body: I loved this app, I looked through so many and tried several of the free versions. This one was great. Then I purchased it and it no longer could find ANY recipes on websites. I mean none. I tried it side by side with other recipe keeper apps and those could find the recipes but not this one.

title: A beautiful app with only one issue
body: After many years of trying all the top recipe managers, I think Mela is absolutely the best. It only has one issue holding it back from perfection, and I'm hopeful the developer will resolve this someday. When importing recipes (regardless of which website) more often than not the fields for Prep Time and Cooking Time do not populate and have to be filled manually. I've tried importing the same recipes using three other highly-rated recipe managers and these fields fill just fine, so it is not a problem with the websites. If you can overlook this, Mela has an absolutely gorgeous UI and a UX that addresses everything you could expect in managing, displaying and printing recipes.

title: Almost perfect
body: Overall a really well-designed app. Feels super simple compared to others like Paprika, which can feel overstuffed with features. All it needs is a better grocery list. Items are not categorized (i.e. Produce, Dairy, etc.), they’re just thrown into a chaotic master list, which means that when I go shopping, I’m constantly flicking up and down the list to find the things in whatever section of the store I’m in.

title: Solid Recipe Manager
body: So far I am enjoying this app. My favorite feature is the numerous ways to add recipes. it makes transitioning to this app seamless. I love being able to import recipes directly from the browser and scanning my recipes from books. I also love being able to import a bunch of recipes from blogs that I want to try in the future. The interface is sleek. The app is intuitive and easy to use. My only issues are with the grocery list section of the app. The good thing about the grocery section is grocery items aren’t automatically added to the list from your meal plan calendar. Instead there is an add to grocery list button on each recipe, which I like because it allows more control for me. What I don’t like: the grocery section is lacking in functionality and features. Spending less time making my grocery list and less time in the grocery store is the goal and right now this part of the app doesn’t cut it. I would like to see a feature where you can have pre defined grocery lists saved and then the ability to add those items to your main grocery list. This way I don’t have to keep adding the same staples that I buy every week. I would also like to see the ability to change the order of the grocery list items with a click and drag feature in order to keep grocery items in the order I would navigate in the store. I would also like to see the ability to add meta data to each grocery item to list which aisle number this is in and then be able to group by aisle number. I would also like to see basic and custom categories (produce, meat, frozen, etc). This would would make my life as a mom who likes to cook from scratch so much easier. I will keep this app for now and hope they make these changes in the future.

title: Feature Request
body: Love the app but wish there was a way to add subcategories or some sort of hierarchy for organizing the recipes.

title: Need easier search
body: Love the app - easy to import recipes. Great formatting and the Cook view is awesome. BUT the only way I’ve found to search is to scroll to the top of the ALL list which can take a lot of strokes on my iPad with nearly 1000 recipes. Please improve this!

title: Great app
body: …but needs a general search mechanism

title: One Feature Request
body: This app is terrific and you should get it if you want an easy way to manage your recipes. I do wish that I could share multiple recipe collections with multiple people. Sharing my mom’s recipes with her and my partner’s recipes with them (without mixing recipes up) would be a huge improvement on the all or nothing approach the app takes now.

title: Almost perfect
body: After quite a lot of research, I landed on Mela about a year ago. Now, I consider it indispensable for reasons you see in others’ reviews: ease of use, layout, the powerful ability to scoop just the needed bits from wordy, ad-filled recipe web pages. It’s truly remarkable that way. One thing that mars the overall experience, however, is that it’s clunky to navigate. For example, it takes a lot of extra touches/clicks to go from recipes in one category to those in another. A simple pop-up list would help simplify navigation. Similarly, I don’t know how many times I’ve searched for a known recipe in my collection and found nothing, only to realize that my search was confined to the category I didn’t realize I was in; make searches global, and one of the few frustration points would be immediately gone. Small but meaningful improvements like these could make an very good experience truly marvelous.

title: I wish it defaulted to “cook” mode
body: The typeface is much more legible in cooking mode, and it’s much more useful to swipe between instructions and ingredients. Paprika’s default typeface is more legible and larger.

title: Wonderful, Aside from Browsing
body: Mela has been the best recipe manager I've used of a few. The interface is clean, without a bunch of multi-step fatigue when choosing recipes. The real shine for Mela is the cooking view. On Mac and iPad you have a persistent pane with your ingredients, and a clear view of directions. You can also add multiple timers on the same screen! Other recipe managers I've used aren't any better than viewing a site, so I appreciate Mela being innovative. If I could change anything about Mela, it would be to allow support for Safari extensions. I don't know whether this is possible, but cooking websites have an aggravating amount of ads and other intrusive data tracking practices. Mela doesn't collect any information, and it would be wonderful if the browser followed the same privacy rules. If I want to support a cooking site I buy their cookbook, online ads are a cancer.

title: Beautiful app for storing recipes
body: This app makes a beautiful and very practical. Designed with iOS first an Feature requests: more nutritional information styling similar to ingredients. The ability to schedule to make a meal with x amount of servings and be able to assign each serving (or multiple servings) to specific days.

title: Great App with a Surprising Shortcoming
body: I really like this app. I purchased both the macOS and iOS versions and have already entered about 900 recipes. I was looking forward to using my phone in the kitchen to follow the recipes as I cooked but found that the iOS version had no way to search for specific recipes. You have to scroll through manually. It’s not a huge hassle, but it is surprising test there is no search function.

title: Great App
body: I moved from paprika and really love the clean UI and great UX. I’m looking forward to the family sharing sync as that is a big deal in my house. Other than that I only wish there was a calendar planning feature like paprika

title: Needs way to save links to recipes it can’t scrape
body: A few recipes I have tried to import via the web simply will not automatically import the actual recipe (sometimes it gets the ingredient list but can’t see the directions. I know web scraping isn’t an exact science and manually retyping every single step on an iPhone is a pain, but maybe having an option to keep web bookmarks with the other recipes for now would be nice.

title: The recipe app to rule them all
body: Not only is this the best cooking/planning/recipe storage app out there, it may just be my favorite app hands down. The scan to upload feature? RSS feeds? Calendar? Grocery list? I cannot say enough good things about it, and I cannot tell enough people about it. Thank you for Mela!

title: By far the best recipe app
body: Almost no notes. The app truly works so seamlessly

title: Best Recipe App Hands Down
body: I have been using this app for a few years now. Literally have hundreds of recipes my family cycles through. The app is beautiful and having the syncing is awesome. You can point it at your grocery list and have the ingredients added to the list. This thing is spot on and well written and well supported. Never had any issues with it. Make sure you do the Mela+ too

title: Fantastic recipe app
body: This is the best recipe app that I’ve used. It’s super simple. The UI is great. It’s really easy to navigate. Nothing feels clustered so the spacing is really good and doesn’t feel overwhelming. Developer did a fantastic job with not going overboard with the features. I feel like a lot of recipe apps tend to add more features than what’s necessary. FEATURE ID LIKE TO REQUEST I would really love to be able to link recipes to other recipes. title: Life changing app
body: This app has honestly changed my cooking life. First off, the interface is beautiful. I’ve seen some recipe apps that look very old school or clunky, and Mela isn’t that. Mela’s cost is a very reasonable one-time fee, unlike a lot of its competitors. (I REFUSE to pay an ongoing subscription to my recipe collection, which is why I ended up downloading Mela in the first place.) It makes meal planning a BREEZE, so I actually -do- meal plan now, and only buy the groceries I’ll use for the week! I’m saving so much money on produce that I would buy and then forget which recipe I was supposed to use it in (and then forget about altogether, so it would rot in the fridge) and I have no more angst about figuring out what to cook for dinner every night. I love having all my recipes in one place, so I’m reminded of recipe options that wouldn’t occur to me otherwise. My family is eating a much wider variety of dishes since Mela. A few suggestions for the developers: I’d love it if there were a way to easily switch between multiple recipes (for times when I’m making a main dish as well as side dishes, all at the same time). I’d love it if the grocery list feature attempted to list similarly-named products near each other (so i can easily see, for example, how much Half & Half I need to buy to cover all 5 of the recipes I’m planning to make for Thanksgiving that call for it, without having to scroll through the whole grocery list, manually find all the half and half entries, and add the quantities together). I’d love it if each entry on the grocery list indicated which recipe the ingredient is for. I’d also love to be able to permanently assign a category to each of the ingredients in a recipe so that when I add them to my grocery list, they show up under a group name like “produce” or “pantry” or “frozen”. (It would be cool if Mela took a stab at assigning a category for each ingredient when the recipe is first added, but let me permanently update any ingredient’s categorization if I want to.) I’d love to be able to search the recipe collection for multi-word terms: for example, “shredded chicken” or “chuck roast”. When I type in two words, it seems to return results that contain either word rather than both words, and putting the words together in quotes results in no results being returned. I’d love it if the “Scan Recipe” feature allowed for scanning a recipe from more than one image, because a lot of recipes I’ve saved are split across two pages. These are just suggestions for the developer, but overall, I love the app and highly, highly recommend it. If you like cooking, or have a family to feed, it’s a no-brainer must have app.
